title: Compressed interface members block approved writes behind a generic pipeline error
symptom: A staged registry built only from the actual 28-key/86-pair answer evaluated 86/86 pairs as approved and writable. All 28 synthetic examples passed public dry-run/apply/check/re-dry-run. Of 19 actual scoped files, 15 were approval-eligible; 12 staged applies succeeded while three eligible dry-runs exited 2 with ALIGN_NOT_ELIGIBLE and the inner message BoxBox alignment failed with exit code 1. Source refusal counts were zero and the failed candidates stayed unchanged.

rootCause.summary: Original 2026-11-14 mechanism, superseded in the local 2026-11-16 candidate: All three failed staged inputs contain compressed interface members, with SUGGEST counts 1, 2 and 1. The TypeScript alignment runner returns 1 before writing when compressed members or unsupported parameters remain. The public TypeScript writer discards the emitted report and wraps this as a generic alignment exit-code failure. The known case is a structural-authoring precondition plus a diagnostic gap, not missing approval, a second-cycle failure or an established safety bug. A generic public CLI pair confirmed this: the approved aligned control succeeds, while adding one compressed interface leaves source Check at exit 0 and approvalEligible=true but makes Align dry-run fail before writing. The inner 1 is an in-process return status, not a spawned child-process exit.

requestedOutcome: Expose the specific compressed-member precondition and direct the authorized owner to Write/Refactor before retrying horizontal Align; verify a minimized add/remove case and preserve refusal, approval and unchanged-source guarantees.
decisions: Keep this separate from missing conventions and the no-op performance mechanism. Approval alone does not resolve all observed failures.
Do not weaken source, parser, token/AST, fixed-point, whole-file approval or atomic-write safeguards to make the three files pass.
No private consumer identifiers or source snippets are published. A generic approved control and compressed addition were observed through the public CLI; both retained their input bytes.
No engine or production source/registry change is implied by the staged results. The larger unapproved key/file set remains outside the recorded answer.

A complete approval proof does not authorize a structural transformation. Compressed interface members must first be expanded through the authorized Write/Refactor workflow, with its own behavior and source checks. Do not force Align past the precondition.
